newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq drops as network stocks slip further.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq drops as network stocks slip further.

text.p: Nasdaq shares finished lower for the third straight session as networking stocks continued to slide and investor nervousness lingered, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index dropped 3.67 points or 0.28 percent to close unofficially at 1308.99. Overall, losing issues beat gainers 2513 to 1817 on total volume of 704 million shares.

"Most of the techs were weak after yesterday's massive selloff. The network players had a bad week. Typically a sell-off would attract bargain hunters the next day, but there was just a lot of uncertainty out there," one trader said.
Networking stocks were slammed in heavy trading during the last two sessions in the wake of the proposed acquisition of modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp by 3Com Corp.

U.S. Robotics lost 3-5/16 to 55-13/16, 3Com shed almost 2 to 33 and Ascend Communications Inc dropped 4-3/4 to 52-1/4. Some large capitalization technology stocks showed some strength. Intel Corp gained 2-9/64 to 141-7/8 and Dell Computer Corp added 1 to 71-1/8.
In other news, Biofield Corp fell 5-3/4 to 4-3/4 after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration rejected its application for a breast cancer diagnosis device.
